extracted.intended_audience: students and teachers of poetry/practical criticism (undergraduate literature students)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reading and judging lyric poems (especially sonnets) focusing on clarity of sense, construction, diction, rhythm, sincerity, and reader technique. Emphasises practical skills of construing and balanced attention to matter and manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intelligibility / clarity of meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: "I find the poem unintelligible as it stands... I cannot reconcile the last two lines. A title would possibly have saved the situation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the poem's sense can be grasped and whether images and lines can be reconciled; inability to construe indicates a substantive defect and points to a need for better reader technique. Note specific opaque phrases (e.g. 'his very urn') and ask if they block understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between expression (envelope) and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The "willingness to accept the envelope in place of the contents" and instances where "expression is otherwise curiously excellent" though thought is obscure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not confuse striking phrasing or polished diction with genuine grasp of the poem's thought; examine whether the style masks a lack of substantive content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compactness and force of thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments like the thought being "compact and forcible" even when the poem seems unintelligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the poem actually contains a compact, forcible idea or merely sounds as if it does; be wary of readers mistaking the sound of compactness for real conceptual compactness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and sonnet-form division
rubrics_metrics.description: "The sonnet, however, is finely constructed... The construction of the sonnet is excellent, as there is a definite division."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate formal features (octave/sestet break, distribution, crescendo) and whether the structural division serves the poem's thought; beware dogmatic adherence to 'definite division' as a teaching snippet rather than a flexible test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence / unity of sentences and argument
rubrics_metrics.description: "A sentence of seven lines... is rather unwieldy and clumsy for a sonnet"; remarks on detachment of phrases and lack of connection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that sentences and syntactical units are connected and that the argument or narrative holds together; long, rambling sentences often create disunity and hinder comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and clarity of imagery / metaphor
rubrics_metrics.description: Difficulties reconciling images: "wrist that fashioned... clay" vs "cast in bronze upon his very urn"; abrupt metaphor introductions are "disconcerting."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine metaphors for compatibility and narrative logic; abrupt or mixed imagery that cannot be reconciled weakens sense and invites reader confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Felicity and clarity of the ending / close
rubrics_metrics.description: "'Cast in bronze upon his very urn' seems unfortunate, bringing one to a sharp stop... 'and for what good reason' is a strikingly prosaic ending."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the final lines resolve the poem's thought, or jolt/seed the meaning in a way that undermines the whole; a weak or prosaic close can spoil an otherwise effective poem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythm and metre as evidence of feeling
rubrics_metrics.description: "The rhythm of the octet is faster... the irregularity of the metre emphasises the sincerity and passion" but "the rhythm test may mislead."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rhythm and metrical behaviour as one clue to sincerity and speaker attitude, but apply only after close engagement with the poem; rhythm can be mimicked and may mislead if considered alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness / naturalness of diction (avoidance of artifice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticisms of "self-conscious" tricks of style, forced words to secure rhyme, and false 'poetic diction' (e.g. 'unimpeachable' used oddly).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether word choice feels genuine to the voice and situation; forced, showy, or unnatural diction suggests striving after effect rather than authentic speech and may damage sincerity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity / genuineness of emotion
rubrics_metrics.description: "Marked by sincerity... not himself convinced... the writer is playing with an idea rather than expressing a conviction."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether the poet genuinely believes or feels what is expressed (deep movement of thought/feeling) rather than merely adopting a pose or rhetorical effect; examine evidence in diction, control, and coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional force sufficient to carry the reader
rubrics_metrics.description: "The feeling is not strong enough to carry the reader along with it"; poems that seem like exercises rather than genuine emotion fail to engage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the poem's emotion is compelling and sustained enough to move readers; weak feeling produces detachment and the impression of artifice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mood / 'state of mind' vs doctrinal truth
rubrics_metrics.description: If poetry expresses a 'state of mind' or 'mood' "the thoughts presented need not be examined on their own account."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a poem is essentially mood-expression, criticism may focus less on the literal truth of propositions and more on how effectively the mood is conveyed; however, incoherence of thought or emotion remains problematic even then.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use (and danger) of stock subjects and comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: "This was the most popular theme... stock subject... Two readers... are as much hindered by their recollections of Keats as the last writer was helped."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert to stock subjects and canonical echoes that can either illuminate or unduly bias response; recollections may help or be stumbling-blocks to fresh construal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical skill: reader's ability to construe
rubrics_metrics.description: "The reader's pathetic distrust of their own power to construe... their inability to work out and grasp the splendid thought... educators will recognise as crucial."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach and practise constructive techniques for making sense of poems; inability to construe is a practical defect that can be remedied by training in ordinary English construing and close reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atmosphere / tone of approach influencing popularity
rubrics_metrics.description: "The confident air of the sonnet, by creating a very favourable 'atmosphere of approach'... was also influential".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise how a poem's confident manner or tone can predispose readers to like it; account for such rhetorical atmosphere when explaining popularity or favourable responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grandiloquence vs precision (avoid unnecessary difficulty)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Grandiloquent rather than grand... obvious truth of the sentiment... wrapt in unnecessary difficulties."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether elevated or ornate language genuinely deepens meaning or merely obscures an otherwise simple truth; unnecessary difficulty is a fault if it hides rather than enhances thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of manner (treatment) and matter (content)
rubrics_metrics.description: "To consider either treatment or content exclusively is a means of keeping at a distance from the actual poem."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism should attend to both how something is said and what is said; isolating form from content (or vice versa) risks missing the poem's full effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vividness of descriptive detail
rubrics_metrics.description: "The description of the woman's beauty [is] not sufficiently vivid and living to make one realise the terrible tragedy."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether imagery and detail are vivid enough to support the poem's claim or emotional effect; weak description can make an argument literal and unconvincing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obscurity as device vs artistic flaw
rubrics_metrics.description: "Sense obscure on first reading... if it lacks limpidity, it does... become a nut to crack... But is it artistically better or worse? Worse — easier to appreciate, but rather a puzzle than a poem."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether obscurity is purposeful and yields reward on closer study, or whether it merely frustrates understanding; enticing difficulty differs from gratuitous puzzlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of specific word choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific criticisms such as "slay, a most unsuitable word" or "unimpeachable suggests a sneer."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate individual lexical choices for tonal fit and semantic appropriateness; a single awkward word can destabilise sense or register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical/contextual plausibility as auxiliary evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: "The mere date of a poem cannot by itself settle its genuineness... it is only a probability... but it is enough to make knowledge of a poem's date a useful aid to judgment."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use period, authorial context, and style as presumptive evidence about sincerity or authenticity, but make final decisions on close textual contact rather than relying solely on external dating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate match of manner (force, virility, tenderness) to matter
rubrics_metrics.description: "The poem leaves one with a sense of strength... 'Of the earth, earthy.' ... absence of least artifice, but natural suggestion of sounds..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the poem's energetic or restrained manner suits its subject-matter; mismatches (e.g. brute force for subtle theme) affect artistic success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of speaker/addressee and dramatic situation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Is the poet addressing a woman, or a statue?... The failure to recognise a sonnet we have met before... reader unaware that his interpretation does not exhaust the possibilities."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify who is speaking to whom and the poetic situation; ambiguous or shifting address can be a legitimate device but often causes confusion that needs resolving in interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound-patterning and small-scale formal shaping (crescendo, alliteration, syllable count)
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is a crescendo... restraint of its language... prevalence of 'S' sounds... quick monosyllables 'will not be lost'... movement quickens."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to how sound, syllable-count, alliteration, and local pacing contribute to emotional movement and meaning; note how shifts in sound-pattern mark rhetorical transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection of posed attitude or 'pose' for effect
rubrics_metrics.description: "I can find no trace of a pose assumed for the writing of the sonnet... One is tempted to inquire what it was that set this writer looking for traces of a pose."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert to signs that the poet is assuming an attitude for display rather than writing from conviction; posed mannerisms can undercut sincerity and require careful weighing against textual evidence.
